Tool or resource page named by the toolkit

description: State Climate Summaries is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by North Carolina Institute for Climate Studies (NCICS). Access summary documents for U.S. States and territories. The summaries cover historical climate variations and trends, future climate model projections of climate conditions during the 21st century, and past and future conditions of sea level and coastal flooding. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Air Quality, Changing Seasons, Drought, Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Extreme Cold, Extreme Heat, Flooding – Coastal, Flooding – Rainfall-induced, High Winds, Landslides, Severe Winter Weather, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems, Vector-Borne Disease, Water Quality, Wildfire. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Aquatic and Marine Resources, Economy, Energy and Utilities, Forestry, Natural Areas and Wildlife, People, Property, Transportation and Mobility, Urban Landscape and Tree Canopy, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
